claims.text: The initial material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with a balanced matrix and stable second-phase particles.
At 500–600 °C, stress-assisted dynamic recrystallization occurs in the alloy.
Dynamic M23C6 carbide or Cr-rich sigma-phase precipitates form along grain boundaries at 500–600 °C under sufficiently high stress.
The grain-boundary precipitates are concomitant with stress-assisted recrystallization.
Dynamic recrystallization and precipitation increase local microstructural heterogeneity.
Grain-boundary precipitates concentrate local mechanical stresses.
Grain-boundary precipitates act as mechanical barriers.
Grain-boundary precipitates disrupt continuous protective oxide or passive films.
Precipitate-associated stress concentration increases localized micro-cracking and material removal.
Passive-film disruption at precipitate sites causes passivation failure and initiates or accelerates pitting.
The combined mechanical and electrochemical effects synergistically accelerate total degradation.
Relative to a matched alloy with a more stable microstructure, the dynamically recrystallized and precipitated alloy will have a higher wear rate.
Relative to the matched baseline, the dynamically recrystallized and precipitated alloy will have a higher corrosion rate, greater pitting, and more pronounced passive-film failure.
Relative to the matched baseline, the dynamically recrystallized and precipitated alloy will have greater total material loss.
Rapid quenching or lower-temperature annealing can suppress dynamic recrystallization and precipitation and thereby preserve a more continuous passive layer.
The proposed mechanism applies when the temperature is around 500–600 °C, the mechanical sliding is continuous, and the corrosive medium has controlled pH and ionic content.
The proposed comparison holds temperature, wear conditions, pH, and ionic composition constant while varying the extent of recrystallization and precipitation.
Failure of the recrystallized and precipitated samples to exhibit significantly higher total, wear, and corrosion degradation than the control would falsify the hypothesis.
